about.title: Pico Rivera Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Pico Rivera's mix of light industrial yards, delivery hubs, and retail corridors along Rosemead Boulevard, Whittier Boulevard, and Slauson Avenue means workplace injuries here often involve forklifts, loading docks, or vehicles moving through busy commercial lots. Because California generally makes workers' compensation the exclusive remedy against an employer, many injured workers assume that's the only path forward. But when a subcontractor, delivery driver, equipment manufacturer, or property owner outside your own employer contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be possible alongside your comp benefits. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured workers in Pico Rivera with an independent attorney who can sort through both angles. There's no cost to you unless the attorney recovers compensation on your behalf. If you were hurt on a job site anywhere in the city, from a warehouse near Paramount Boulevard to a retail loading zone off Slauson, it's worth having someone review the full picture.

whyChoose.title: Why Injured Workers in Pico Rivera Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Untangle Comp vs. Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or another driver can open a separate claim. An attorney in our network can help determine whether your case involves both.

items.title: We Understand the 30-Day Reporting Window
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report a workplace injury to their employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so we connect you quickly with someone who can advise on next steps.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Matters
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job, an attorney can explain your protections under California law.

items.question: I was hurt working at a warehouse off Rosemead Boulevard by a delivery truck driver who wasn't my coworker. Can I still file a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. If the driver worked for a different company or was an independent contractor, that may support a third-party injury claim separate from your workers' comp benefits. An attorney can review the details and let you know which claims apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer?
items.answer: California generally requires you to notify your employer within 30 days of a workplace injury. Reporting promptly helps preserve your workers' comp rights, so it's best not to wait.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury in Pico Rivera?
items.answer: No, retaliation for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney in our network can talk through your options at no cost to you.
